title: Road/Trail Run in Yangmingshan National Park
notes:
Wrong bus stop -> Zhuzihu-> Xiaomenkeng-> Qixing Mountain-> Lengshuikeng-> 7-11-> Kawayu Bathhouse

Longest run in a while. Ran few miles up to Zhuzihu before going through a forest up to the peak of Qixing. Dark by the time I got to the top. Ran down and found the nearest 7-11, finished the night with a Japanese style bathhouse a few miles away. Very rainy and foggy weather. Very cool trails and the misty weather left either a magical or insidious atmosphere. Switchbacks do not exist in Taiwan, only staircases straight up the rock. This was so cool!

title: Halls Creek Narrows
notes:
64,000 step day

Up the road, down into the canyon, along the river wash, into the narrows, over Halls Divide, back along the river wash to camp. Water got up to my waist in the narrows but no further. Got lost a few times, particularly getting in and out over the narrows and over the divide. My feet hurt. Spectacular trail. Exceptionally eerie, everything was incredibly still unless the wind made the trees rustle. Didn’t see a soul except the jackrabbit that leapt out at the trailhead. Last person on the trail was 11/20. Sand near the river was very fine and sunk me to my knees a couple times. Misjudged mileage and the sun set before I was out of the narrows. Fantastic day. Bedrock tabi socks are a godsend

title: Out of Halls Creek Narrows trail
notes: Limped out of this. Overdid it the day before, had sores on top of my foot and my right index toe was messed up. Made a probably poor decision to climb out of a notch in the canyon wall on the right and it was a bit dicey, several scramble moves in no fall zones. God bless whoever left cairns indicating the easiest climbing route. Popped out of the canyon wall and trekked a few miles to the road and to my car. Knocked off several miles. Success!

title: Hike in to Pioneer Yurt; Peanut
Hyndman Peak Attempt
notes:
6-7 hour day of brutality and a ton of fun 

Ty Randall and I decided to bootpack to the saddle rather than straight up the couloir which proved to be a mistake. We were greeted with a knife’s edge ridge and a vertical rock face barring us from summitting from the ridge, so we had to traverse back over, navigating rock, ice and snow. By the time we made it to the main chute, Brinton and Ike were skiing down and we decided to join rather than summit and risk the snow getting icier. Overall awesome, brutal day with some amazing views.  Would love to come back to this peak in the spring.

title: Monument Valley 50k
notes:
Stopped watch late, time was 7:08, pace of 13.02 min miles

Holy smokes this was so awesome. Other than the 7 hours of running best day of my life. Shoutout to my mom for coming 😸

Monument Valley basically closed for the day for the event, and the route took us through trails that are normally only accessible by Navajo guide, so I felt so lucky to see so much amazing stuff. Tribal music was playing before we started the race and MV is genuinely one of the most insane places I’ve ever seen. Was in complete awe for most of the run. Vast desert valleys surrounded by incredible buttes. Mitchell Mesa climb was a highlight. 

Everyone was so nice and saying good job to each other on the trail it was awesome. I had so much fun eating gummy bears and listening to PinkPantheress. Dill pickle chips at mile 11 were the most insane things I’ve ever tasted 

The course was 3 varying sized loops that were all spectacular in their own right. I think I’m partial to the last loop, miles 21-29

I got sick a couple days ago and was definitely feeling it but I could at least breathe through my nose. Miles 16-21 were genuinely rough, but felt much better for the final 11ish. Probably went a little to quick miles 1-6. I got like full face chills around mile 13 which wasn’t fun 

Mountain Dew and Sprite at mile 21 were insane. The amount of salt accumulation on my hat was awesome. Definitely underestimated the difficulty of the route, it was sandy the whole time and had more hills than I anticipated

So much fun!  One of the most beautiful areas I’ve ever seen

title: Lone Peak
notes:
Absolutely brutal day with Jude and Parker. Started around 11:30 pm and ended around 11:30 am. 16 miles and 6k vert in 12 hours. 10 of the miles were in the worst snow ever that would sink us past our knees, making it grueling to get anywhere. Seriously one of the most brutal days I’ve ever had outside 

We were worried about summiting due to the snow condition, but it ended up working out alright. The walk along the top ridge was so awesome. 

Big awesome day and so much fun mountaineering and really happy with our effort. I didn’t sleep at all so battling crazy fatigue. But mile 13 hot tamales and ibuprofen pulled through

title: Grand Teton Summit via Owen-Spaulding
notes:
Watch died before summit, but ~15 miles and 7000+ ft of elevation gain. Bucket list day!! 

We started at 1:45 am and didn’t finish till 8:15 pm. 18 and a half hour day had me dead 

Fun climbing at the top, absolutely brutal trail the whole way. Idk if I’d do it in one day again, would definitely split it into 2 

Beautiful epic day! So glad Caleb and Ethan could join me 

Roped up for Bellyroll and Owen’s Chimney, solo’d the rest. Rapping down was great, I would not have felt comfortable down climbing a couple of these sections.
